questions.title: The Direct Method
questions.subtitle: Direct dough preparation
answers: It's a preparation method simpler than indirect methods.
All ingredients are incorporated directly and after a more or less long rest it can be used.

questions.title: Poolish

answers: Poolish is a pre-fermentation of the dough that rests for several hours before being used for pizza dough.
It is prepared by mixing 1 part flour and 1 part water as well as a small amount of yeast.
It's an indirect method of pizza dough preparation.

questions.title: Yeasts
questions.subtitle: Here we use 3 types of yeasts
answers: Dry active yeast is the yeast found in commerce in the form of "classic" baker's yeast and not rapid. Generally sold in sachets of small pellets.
Dry instant yeast is freeze-dried yeast in the form of fine flakes. It doesn't need to be hydrated before use and allows for quick rises.
Fresh yeast is the yeast found in commerce in the form of "fresh" baker's yeast in the form of paste in cubes.

tips.title: 💡 Tip:
tips.description: The calculator easily allows switching to one or the other of the yeasts

questions.title: 💦 Hydration
questions.subtitle: Ratio between the total amount of water over the total amount of flour
answers: Ex 1: For 100 g of total water I will have 151.5 g of total flour which gives a dough hydration of 66%. Calculation: 100 ÷ 151.5 = 0.66 or 66%.
Ex 2: If I want to know the amount of water to add when I have 151.5 g of flour and I want 66% hydration the calculation will be: 0.66 x 151.5 = 100 g of total water to add.

tips.title: 💡 Tip:
tips.description: The more hydrated the dough, the more difficult it will be to handle, it will be more liquid and therefore stickier. Recommended hydration: Between 62 & 75%

questions.title: 🍚 Poolish Ratio
questions.subtitle: Ratio between the amount of poolish and the total amount of dough
answers: We commonly use between 30 and 60% poolish in the final dough quantity.

Ex: If I want 30% poolish in my dough and 1 kg of final dough, the calculation will be: 1000 x 0.3 = 300 g. The poolish will therefore be 300 g and will be composed of 150 g of flour and 150 g of water.

tips.title: 💡 Tip:
tips.description: Generally we put a higher ratio of poolish in winter than in summer because fermentation is partly influenced by temperature. So putting more poolish in winter than summer can help the final development of the dough.
